info.name: Ecom - Checkout & Rewards Service
info.description:
Full API collection for the Go/Postgres checkout and rewards service.

**Setup**: start the service with `make up && make run` (listens on :8080), then import the
`Ecom - Local` environment or rely on the collection variables below.

**Money**: every amount is integer PAISE (1 rupee = 100 paise). Rs 899.00 is 89900.

**Rewards are per user**: every n of a *user's own* orders earns *that user* one coupon,
redeemable only by them.

**Suggested order**: run folders 00 -> 07 top to bottom. Requests chain through collection
variables (cartId, orderId, couponCode) which are set automatically by test scripts.

**Concurrency**: Postman is a poor fit for proving race behaviour. The real proof is the Go
test suite (`make test`) - concurrent checkouts on limited stock, concurrent redemption of one
coupon, concurrent admin coupon generation, and retried checkouts. To get a feel for it here,
run the collection with newman in several parallel processes.

item.name: 05 Reward flow (per user)
item.description:
Rewards are PER USER and MINTED AUTOMATICALLY: the payment that completes a user's nth paid order issues their coupon in the same transaction. There is no manual generation step.

This folder is self-driving and safe to re-run: 'Check progress' reuses an available coupon if one exists, otherwise it loops place-order-and-pay until the milestone mints one.

item.name: 07 Error contract
item.description:
Every failure returns {code, message} with a stable machine-readable code. Each request here provokes one specific code - run the folder to see the whole error contract.

Run folders 04 and 05 first: the last two requests need a checked-out cart and a coupon owned by another user.

item.name: 08 Payment failure and cancellation
item.description: Payment failure and cancellation. Both must give back whatever the pending order was holding: its stock, and its coupon.

request.description: A cart for the failure path.
The webcam has only 3 units, so the reservation is easy to observe.
Stock leaves the shelf NOW, not at payment. That is what stops ten people paying for the last item.
Inventory has already dropped, before any payment.
The provider declines. The order fails and the reservation is released.
The released reservation is visible immediately.
Now the cancellation path.
A pending order releases both its stock and (if used) its coupon.
A terminal order cannot be cancelled again.
